title: How Cisco Got Bullwhipped
author: Asianometry
note: In the late 1990s, Cisco sat at the heart of the Internet boom - selling networking equipment like routers and switches. To demonstrate the Internet’s revolutionary potential, Cisco made itself into the nimble, fast-moving corporation of the future. A highly praised e-commerce website. Rapid, daily financial reports. And sophisticated data sharing with outsourcing manufacturers. All made possible with the web. So as the Telecom bubble began to implode, Cisco management felt confident enough to double down. They got bullwhipped. In this video, we look at how Cisco misread the signals.

title: We now have Kerr’s Law (Changelog Interviews #689)
author: Changelog Master Feed
note: Dave Kerr created hacker laws, and now he finds himself reviewing agent-written code for them. Back on the show after six years, Dave names what he sees limiting teams today: keeping everyone’s mental model in sync with what’s actually been built. Adam declares it Kerr’s Law on the spot. We get into why Dave’s team treats code review as a deliberate slowdown, how Shellwright lets agents bring evidence to a pull request, and what living with bipolar disorder has taught Dave about noticing when the excitement of these tools stops being healthy.

title: Making Agents Ship in Complex Brownfield Codebases | Dex Horothy, CEO of HumanLayer
author: The Modern Software Developer
note: In this episode of The Build System, I sit down with Dex, CEO of HumanLayer, father of the term “context engineering”, and one of the most prominent thought leaders in the AI coding ecosystem. We break down how teams are actually building with AI today, beyond demos and hype. The conversation digs into why most agent workflows don’t hold up in production, and what changes when you’re working inside large, messy, brownfield systems. We cover: - why most “agent” examples online fail in real environments - the gap between teams seeing ~15–30% gains and those reaching 2–3x productivity - why coding itself is not the main bottleneck in software engineering - the risks of pushing too far toward fully autonomous systems - how AI is starting to reshape team structure and ownership A big theme throughout is that the real leverage comes from improving the entire workflow around coding, not just ge
